analysis.title: Valvoline Inc. (VVV): 4Q26 Earnings Recap: 4Q in line and FY27 outlook better than feared; Repurchases to resume
key_insights: 4Q26 results met expectations. GS says the FY27 outlook was better than feared: strong ticket growth is expected to offset flat same-store transactions, and SG&A leverage is expected to limit the gross margin headwind from elevated product costs.

Same-store transactions were flat to slightly up in 4Q26, a deceleration from the low single-digit contribution in recent quarters. Management expects same-store transactions to be roughly flat y/y through FY27. Ticket growth is expected to be the sole driver of same-store sales growth.
The transaction headwind is mainly reduced new customer acquisition in lower-income markets. GS says stores in more affluent markets are likely also seeing slower customer growth, to a lesser extent.

Customer retention continues to improve and the company sees no sign of trade-out to lower-cost service providers. GS notes the FY27 same-store sales outlook relies on retention holding up while higher costs are passed on, and expects more promotions, discounting and marketing if retention weakens.

SG&A was much better than expected in 4Q26. Valvoline generated leverage in advertising, payroll and other G&A over the past three quarters. Management expects efficiencies to remain a tailwind and SG&A leverage to help offset about 100 bps of expected gross margin pressure in FY27.

Gross margin pressure is concentrated in 1H FY27, with a 200-250 bps headwind, before lapping higher material costs and prices in 2H, mostly 4Q. GS models a gross margin recovery starting in 4Q27 and continuing through FY28, dependent on the supply environment.

Valvoline plans to restart share repurchases in FY27 under its $500mn authorization. GS expects a mix of programmatic and opportunistic buying funded by free cash flow, with no added leverage and no material increase in growth capex, since the company is already near its target of about 100 company-operated stores per year.
GS models $100mn of buybacks in FY27 and $200mn in each of FY28 and FY29.

GS raises FY27 adj. EBITDA to $614.5mn from $613.1mn, as lower gross margin is offset by a better SG&A rate. FY28 adj. EBITDA falls to $715.7mn from $717.8mn on lower sales from a lower store growth outlook. FY29 adj. EBITDA is introduced at $786.1mn.

GS keeps a Buy rating and raises its 12-month price target to $46 from $45 on a roll forward to higher combined 1Q28-4Q28 adj. EBITDA. The downside/base/upside EV/EBITDA multiples are unchanged at 9x/10x/12x.

market_movers.rationale: GS raises its price target to $46 from $45 on a roll forward to higher 1Q28-4Q28 adj. EBITDA, with valuation multiples unchanged. It sees the FY27 outlook as better than feared, with SG&A leverage offsetting gross margin pressure.

earnings_insights: 4Q26 (reported 11/19/2026) met expectations per GS. Same-store transactions were flat to slightly up and SG&A was much better than expected.

GS FY27 estimates (new vs old): adj. EBITDA $614.5mn vs $613.1mn, adj. EPS $1.97 vs $1.90, net revenues $2,321.7mn vs $2,309.5mn, system-wide same-store sales growth 6.2% vs 4.9%. These are GS estimates, not consensus.

GS FY28 estimates (new vs old): adj. EBITDA $715.7mn vs $717.8mn, adj. EPS $2.51 vs $2.44, net revenues $2,514.5mn vs $2,520.1mn. FY29 introduced: adj. EBITDA $786.1mn, adj. EPS $2.89, net revenues $2,721.8mn.
GS 1Q27 estimates: adj. EPS $0.38 (from $0.33), net revenues $546.0mn, adj. EBITDA $132.8mn, gross margin 34.9%, down 250 bps y/y. The EPS figure is a GS estimate.
FY27 gross margin is guided to about 100 bps of pressure, with a 200-250 bps headwind in 1H before lapping in 2H. GS models FY27 gross margin at 36.7%, down 101 bps, and FY28 at 38.3%, up 165 bps.
risk_factors: A persistent, rapid rise in material costs.
Slower-than-expected unit growth or an impairment of long-term growth potential.
Lower-than-expected sales if growth at mature stores slows, new stores cannibalize existing locations, Valvoline loses market share, or non-oil change penetration declines.
Execution or other headwinds weighing on top line growth and long-term profitability.
Flat same-store transactions leave the outlook dependent on retention holding while costs are passed through.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong ticket growth is expected to offset flat same-store transactions. Customer retention keeps improving, there is no sign of trade-out to lower-cost providers, and SG&A leverage limits the gross margin headwind.
tension_points.bear_case: Ticket growth is the sole expected driver of same-store sales growth, so the outlook relies on retention holding while higher costs are passed on. New customer acquisition is weak in lower-income markets and likely softer in affluent ones.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weakening in customer retention or shifting transaction/traffic trends, which GS expects would force more promotions, discounting and marketing.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong ticket growth and SG&A leverage should offset flat transactions and elevated product costs, and customer retention continues to improve.
theme_stances.evidence: FY27 outlook came in better than feared
